859e52f1790f4b91: KUALA LUMPUR: Applications for all categories of domestic and overseas postal voting for the 16th Melaka election opened today.
Election Commission (EC) secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus said all applications must be submitted online via the MySPR portal, with the closing date to be announced later.
"Eligible voters who intend to cast their ballots by post must register for or have an existing MySPR account before submitting their application," he said in a statement today.
Khairul Shahril said Category 1A applications covered police and military personnel, election officials, EC members and staff, as well as media personnel.
Applications are also open under Category 1B for Malaysians residing abroad and Category 1C for agencies or organisations.
For further enquiries, applicants can contact the EC hotline at 03-8892 7080 or email upup@spr.gov.my.

Yesterday, Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh announced the dissolution of the Melaka Legislative Assembly, effective today, paving the way for the 16th Melaka election following the consent of Yang Dipertua Negeri Tun Mohd Ali Rustam.
Melaka Legislative Assembly Speaker Datuk Ibrahim Durum also submitted the dissolution notice to the EC yesterday.

In the 2021 Melaka election, Barisan Nasional (BN) won 21 of the 28 seats to form the state government with a more than two-thirds majority, while Pakatan Harapan secured five seats and Perikatan Nasional two.
2cc50fba3123e2b7: KUALA LUMPUR: The wife of senior fire officer Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, who remains missing after flash floods struck Nepal, said she has come to terms with whatever fate awaits her husband.
Hani Othman said she and her family had resigned themselves to fate after 29 days of enduring a deeply trying period.
"Whatever fate God has for my husband, whether he returns to our family or returns to his creator, my family and I accept it.
"My hope now is for the best possible outcome for my husband and peace for our family. If permitted by God, I will return to Nepal. I will continue what my husband was doing before this," she said.
Hani had travelled to Kathmandu on her own initiative to seek updates on the search for her husband and members of his group who remained untraceable following the disaster.

While there, she shared regular updates on her efforts to locate her husband and other Malaysians, including visiting hospitals in Nepal to assist with body identification and distributing aid to victims alongside local non-governmental organisations.

Fakhrul, also known as Loe, was reported missing after the four-wheel-drive carrying his Everest Base Camp expedition group along the Tibet route was believed to have been swept away by massive floods and landslides in a valley in Rasuwa.
A total of 55 Malaysians were reported missing following the Aug 26 disaster.
Hani said since returning to Malaysia on Sept 12, she had continued gathering information about her husband through his personal computer, old phone and documents.
"To calm myself, I spend time performing prayers, reading the Quran and listening to lectures on YouTube. I have also received various forms of support from family and friends," she said.
Asked what she hoped for, Hani said she wanted a definitive answer about her husband's fate.

"Having been there for 15 days, I fully understand the situation and the challenges faced by the government. Although I know that only God can help in this situation, I hope the search efforts continue where possible. There will be no results without physical effort," she said.
Hani also urged other affected families to continue praying, remain strong and accept God's decree.
"I deeply understand how heavy these days are for them. No words are comforting enough to erase this yearning and grief.
"May we all be granted extraordinary patience by God to remain resilient through this trial. God willing, we can endure this test together," she said.

bff4b198b691d319: KUALA LUMPUR: The Real Estate and Housing Developers' Association (Rehda) Malaysia has called on the government to introduce a special Home Ownership Campaign (HOC) next year to tackle the issue of existing unsold completed residential units.
This campaign would specifically target unsold completed units that have received a certificate of completion and compliance (CCC).

The association notes that while the National Housing Policy (DRN) 2026-2035 aims to improve the alignment of supply and demand through data-driven planning, immediate intervention is necessary to absorb current unsold stock.
A special HOC would complement long-term reforms, improve market liquidity, and enable capital to be recycled into new developments, the association said in its 2027 budget wishlist released today.

The association also highlighted that while many prospective buyers may have the capacity to service monthly repayments, upfront acquisition costs remain a hurdle, as they may face difficulty accumulating sufficient savings for stamp duty and other charges and fees.

Recognizing this challenge to prospective home buyers, Rehda suggested extending the current stamp duty relief to residential properties priced above RM500,000 and up to RM1 million, through an appropriate tiered relief mechanism for purchases made between January and December 2027.

In addition to that, access to end-financing is also identified as a major barrier, especially for young Malaysians, the self-employed, gig-economy workers, and those with variable or non-traditional incomes, noted Rehda.
The association proposed expanding and enhancing the Skim Jaminan Kredit Perumahan (SJKP) and other government-backed housing financing or guarantee mechanisms.
Furthermore, the association suggested improving step-up financing structures that offer lower repayments during the initial years of homeownership.
Rehda also emphasized that housing affordability is affected by the cost of developing and delivering homes, not just purchasers' access to financing.
Rising infrastructure, utility, statutory, regulatory, and compliance costs cumulatively impact project viability and housing affordability.

To address this, Rehda proposed for a review of government-imposed costs and regulatory requirements affecting residential development, including infrastructure, utility, statutory, regulatory, and compliance-related charges.
The association also called for the government to avoid introducing new or increased charges without considering their cumulative impact on housing affordability.
Rehda also called for affordability impact assessments for major new policies, regulations, standards and charges affecting residential development.
Meanwhile, the association noted that high initial investment required for modern construction technologies remains a barrier to adoption, particularly for small and medium-sized developers.

There are significant upfront costs associated with Building Information Modelling (BIM), Industrialised Building System (IBS), artificial intelligence (AI), automation, software, equipment, system integration, and training.

To encourage the adoption of the modern construction technology, Rehda proposes for targeted fiscal incentives, inclusing provision of accelerated capital allowance or investment tax allowance for qualifying BIM, IBS, AI, automation, software, and equipment expenditure.
It also called for enhanced or double tax deductions for qualifying implementation, integration, cybersecurity, training, and professional certification costs.

While sustainable housing and green building practices are becoming the norm, Rehda noted that existing green incentives do not adequately benefit all property segments, especially residential developments built for sale.

It also noted that the current green investment tax allowances (GITA) claim process is relatively restrictive, and higher green standards often entail additional upfront costs for both developers and purchasers.

To address this, Rehda proposed for the broadening of fiscal incentives for green property development by extending the existing GITA and green income tax exemption schemes for a further 10 years to provide long-term policy certainty and encourage sustained investment.

232e91845f3f854b: LONDON: The dollar rose to its strongest level in two months on Wednesday on prospects of interest rate hikes in the near term, although easing oil prices could alter the global inflation and monetary policy outlook.

The euro fell to its lowest since late July and was last down 0.25 per cent at US$1.142. Sterling was down 0.3 per cent at US$1.3305. The dollar index, which measures the US currency against six others, was 0.24 per cent higher at 100.79.

The recent barrage of rate hikes and hawkish rhetoric from major central banks has taken centre stage in currency markets as the US-Israeli conflict with Iran drives oil prices higher and fans inflation worries.

Investors are now anticipating further rate rises and a number of Federal Reserve officials have this week signalled more policy tightening may be forthcoming if inflation does not subside quickly enough.
"It's another sign that the Fed story is dominant, and the hawkish Fedspeak is enough to keep USD in demand," ING strategist Francesco Pesole said.

Oil markets remain in the spotlight. Brent crude futures edged back above US$99 a barrel, breaking a five-day stretch of declines that was built on hopes that diplomacy at the UN General Assembly could pave the way for a resolution to the seven-month-long Middle East war.
Brent futures have risen 37 per cent since the conflict erupted at the end of February, while physical prices are at least 75 per cent higher in Europe and at least 40 per cent higher in the US.

"Whether this evolves into a more sustained decline remains to be seen. From a rates perspective, oil floating around the US$90-100/bbl range is unlikely to force a dovish rethink in market expectations," Pesole said.

Crude may be off its recent peaks, but refined product prices are still sky-high. The cost of diesel, which powers most transport, has shot to record highs in the US and to multi-year highs in Europe.
US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday he backed the idea of a diesel export ban as a way to lower domestic prices - something analysts say could do more harm than good to global supply flows.

In his speech at the UN on Tuesday, Trump warned that he could annihilate Iran if there is no deal to end the war, but also suggested an agreement could come soon as diplomatic efforts continued in New York.

"The good news is that oil prices have moderated somewhat from the highs but the path forward remains unclear given the lack of clarity around a possible resolution of the conflict," said Michael Wan, a currency analyst at MUFG.
Investors are also waiting for a high-stakes meeting between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping as the two leaders seek stability in a relationship under pressure over wide-ranging issues.

The Japanese yen was at 157.8 per dollar as traders remain wary of the threat of intervention after the Bank of Japan's rate hike to a 31-year high last week fell short of reassuring investors that more increases may be on the way.
Japanese markets are closed for a holiday and this period of lower liquidity is seen by analysts as an optimal time for authorities to intervene, if needed.

"160 (per US dollar) remains the risk, but officials have reportedly moved away from telegraphing intervention and from any fixed level, so the cap could come earlier and in other forms," Intouch's Williams said.
6e8cacee99f2ec69: KUALA LUMPUR: Talented filmmaking brothers Iskander and Feisal Azizuddin are taking their company, Feisk Productions, to the next level after being selected for a prestigious international film residency in Los Angeles.

The co-founders are among nine Malaysians chosen for the 2026 Global Media Makers (GMM) LA Residency. Running from Sept 12 to Oct 3, the programme connects film and television professionals from Asia with the US industry.

Organised by Film Independent in partnership with the US Department of State's Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs, GMM offers tailored mentorship, expert masterclasses, and hands-on project development.
During the residency, the brothers will focus on their upcoming feature film, Curi Makan (internationally titled Ali & Ben's Spicy Meats).
The family conflict drama premiered at the Blue Chair Film Festival in Laos in 2024 and was recently acquired by Kuala Lumpur-based Abnormal Studios for worldwide sales.
The residency places Iskander and Feisal alongside seasoned filmmakers from across Asia, including those with experience at major global festivals.
International participants include Thai producer Kissada Kamyoung (9 Temples to Heaven) and Indonesian director Khozy Rizal (Little Rebels Cinema Club).

The Malaysian delegation also features strong local talent, such as Fareeq Alias—whose project Pekik won Best Documentary at the 33rd Festival Filem Malaysia—and Zan Azlee, a journalist and documentary filmmaker known for his non-fiction work across Asia and the Middle East.
9879716ecc0f9361: UK utility provider Southern Water is turning fiber-optic telecoms cables into underground sensors in an effort to find leaks in its water network. The privatized biz is trialing tech from Lightsonic that uses Openreach's fiber network to detect leaking pipes. Openreach - BT's infrastructure arm - and Affinity Water, which supplies parts of southern England, tested the system in March. As The Register reported at the time, the system analyzes tiny changes in light traveling through fiber-optic cables to detect vibrations caused by nearby underground leaks. Machine learning helps distinguish those signals from traffic, roadworks and other background noise, and estimates where the water is escaping. Lightsonic says the resulting location data allows engineers to investigate and repair leaks more quickly. It claims the tech is already preventing the loss of more than four million liters (about a million gallons) of water per day across 650 km (400 miles) of the UK's water network. Southern Water is adopting the technology after one of Britain's hottest and driest summers on record, with almost three-quarters of England officially under drought conditions. Southern England is among the country's most water-stressed regions. The utility said Lightsonic's work with Affinity Water and Openreach influenced its decision to run the trial. Southern Water hopes the trial will help it meet Ofwat's leakage-reduction targets for 2030 and strengthen its drought resilience by easing pressure on reservoirs and water abstraction. The company provides water and wastewater services across parts of Hampshire, the Isle of Wight, West Sussex, East Sussex, and Kent. "We've reduced leakage across our network for three consecutive years and continue to invest in innovative techniques and technologies to find and fix leaks even more effectively," said Wayne Novelli, Southern Water's leakage and network strategy manager. "We've been impressed by the leakage reduction metrics and proven success of Lightsonic's technology and are looking forward to working with the team to trial a new way of detecting and tackling them." Southern Water's efforts to conserve clean water come against a less flattering record on wastewater. A court this week fined it £2.4 million ($3.1 million) over several pollution incidents in Kent. That followed a £7.1 million ($9.4 million) fine in July for illegal sewage discharges that forced beaches in Thanet to close. Both prosecutions were brought by the Environment Agency. ®

d8d822c485bad5aa: PETALING JAYA: Pakatan Harapan is expected to announce its candidates for the Melaka state election one to two weeks before nomination day, said the prime minister’s political secretary, Azman Abidin.
Azman said this would allow PH to prepare early instead of waiting until the last minute to finalise its candidates, Bernama reported.
“This time, we are better prepared to name our candidates,” he told reporters after visiting beneficiaries under the Ziarah Kasih programme at the Kuala Linggi state constituency here today.

ba5518f65b172736: MADRID: Former Mexico coach Javier Aguirre will return to Spain to take over at La Liga strugglers Valencia, the club announced on Wednesday.
The 67-year-old led co-hosts Mexico to the 2026 World Cup last 16, where they lost to England, to cap his third spell in charge of his national team.
Aguirre last coached in Spain with Real Mallorca, whom he led to their first Copa del Rey final in 21 years before leaving in 2024.
"The Mexican coach joins until the end of the current season and the club will have an option to extend his contract for one additional season," Valencia said in a statement.
Valencia have mustered just four points from their opening seven league matches of the season to sit second-bottom in the table.
The club, owned by Singaporean billionaire Peter Lim, sacked previous coach Carlos Corberan and CEO Ron Gourlay earlier this month.
The six-time Spanish champions -- lastly in 2004 under Rafael Benitez -- have not finished higher than ninth in La Liga since the 2018/19 season.
Valencia fans have protested heavily against Lim and his son Kiat, who has been club president since March 2025.
Aguirre has previously coached Leganes, Espanyol and Real Zaragoza in Spain.
He took Osasuna to a surprise Champions League qualification with a fourth-placed La Liga finish in 2006 before leaving for Atletico Madrid.
He has also coached the Japan and Egypt national teams.
2a00c04e31f3dd41: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — Malaysia has reached the halfway mark of its six-gold target at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games after collecting three gold and five bronze medals so far.

National Sports Council (NSC) director-general Jefri Ngadirin said the three gold medals had given the Malaysian contingent strong momentum, but cautioned athletes against becoming complacent with many events still to come.
He reminded the athletes that each had an opportunity to contribute to the national contingent.

“Congratulations to all the athletes who have contributed medals to the country. This proves that their hard work, together with their coaches, associations and the entire support team behind them, has paid off.

“Every point, every second and every opportunity matters. We want to see all our athletes give their best, fight until the very end and carry the Malaysian spirit into every competition,” he said in a statement today.
Jefri also called on Malaysians to continue supporting and praying for the national athletes competing in Aichi-Nagoya.
Malaysia’s first gold was delivered by karate exponent Adeola Fay Robert, who won the women’s under-55kg individual kumite event yesterday.

Today, esports athlete Taj Izrin Aiman Taj Madira secured the country’s second gold with victory in the Gran Turismo 7 eRacing event, while karate exponent Shahmalarani Chandran added Malaysia’s third gold in the women’s under-50kg individual kumite.

Malaysia has also bagged five bronze medals, each by Thevendran Kaliana Sundram in the men’s under-55kg individual kumite, Sureeya Shankar Hari Shankar in the men’s under-60kg individual kumite, the men’s team kata squad, Tan Cheong Min in the women’s nanquan and nandao wushu event, and Clement Ting Su Wei in the men’s daoshu and gunshu wushu event. — Bernama
6c3468038d75f179: KANGAR: A housewife who confronted her husband over his frequent late-night outings was slapped, headbutted and choked, at a house in Kampung Permatang Pauh, Simpang Empat, here.

Kangar police chief Assistant Commissioner Yusharifuddin Mohd Yusop said the incident, which occurred around 9.30pm was believed to have stemmed from a misunderstanding between the 49-year-old victim and her 56-year-old husband, who works as a lorry driver.
He said the woman had earlier confronted her husband and asked him not to leave the house at night as she suspected he wanted to meet another woman.
"The suspect became angry after his wife accused him of having another woman and slapped the left side of her face before headbutting her on the forehead.

"The victim, who tried to defend herself, scratched the suspect's shoulder. However, the suspect pushed her, causing her to fall onto a sofa in the living room, before attempting to choke her," he said in a statement today.
Yusharifuddin said the altercation was brought under control by the victim's daughter, who was in the kitchen and heard the commotion in the living room, before the victim fled into the bedroom.
"Further investigations found that the woman had been abused by her husband for almost two years and claimed that she had previously been beaten unconscious.
"Following the latest incident, the victim suffered bruising to her abdomen and was advised to seek treatment and further examination at Tuanku Fauziah Hospital (HTF), Kangar.
"Police arrested the suspect to assist investigations and he has been remanded for four days until Sept 26.
"The case is being investigated under Section 323 of the Penal Code and Section 18 of the Domestic Violence Act," he said.
9656c7b10eda130e: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian property developers continue to face considerable pressure from rising costs, financing constraints, and uncertainties in the wider economic environment, according to Rehda Malaysia president Datuk Zaini Yusoff.

While launch and sales numbers continue to hold up in the first half of the year, Zaini noted that the continuing challenges surrounding end-financing and affordability remain a particular concern among property developers, as costs continue to rise.

"Housing affordability should not be viewed solely from the perspective of property prices. Apart from access to appropriate end-financing, the cost of producing and delivering housing must also form part of the affordability equation," said Zaini in a statement released by Rehda today.
Cost pressures were widespread during the first half of 2026, with 81 per cent of survey respondents reporting an increase in the cost of doing business.
Of those respondents, 35 per cent experienced cost increases of between three and six per cent.

These findings were outlined in the Real Estate and Housing Developers' Association (Rehda) Property Industry Survey for the first half of 2026 and Market Outlook for the second half of 2026 and first half of 2027, which gathered responses from 181 Rehda members across Peninsular Malaysia to assess industry performance.

According to the survey, developers reported an average 13 per cent increase in construction costs between March and June 2026, which was attributed to rising fuel prices and ongoing geopolitical uncertainties.
During 1H 2026, 63 per cent of respondents encountered construction-related challenges, specifically involving building materials and labor.
The wider economic environment directly impacted operations, with 62 per cent of respondents indicating that economic conditions had affected their businesses.

In response to these pressures, developers implemented cost-cutting measures, including freezing recruitment, reducing employee benefits, and retrenchment, with 63 per cent of respondents expecting their companies to freeze hiring between July 2026 and June 2027, Rehda found.
Companies also rescheduled planned launches, delayed projects due to poor demand, and reduced the scale of their launches, said Rehda.
Financing constraints remain a primary hurdle, contributing to a high number of unsold properties.
As of June 30, 59 per cent of respondents reported having unsold completed residential units, the survey found.
The three main reasons cited for these unsold units were end-financing loan rejection, high property prices, and unreleased Bumiputera units.

The main factors contributing to housing loan rejections included purchasers' income eligibility, lower margins of financing offered by financial institutions, and applicants' adverse credit histories.
Despite these pressures, Zaini observed a consistency in launch numbers and a modest improvement in sales, suggesting that market demand is still present.
During 1H 2026, 54 respondents launched 15,834 units, remaining broadly unchanged from the 15,841 units recorded in 2H 2025.

Sales performance saw a 3.2 per cent increase, moving from 5,098 units in 2H 2025 to 5,260 units in 1H 2026. This brought the overall take-up rate up to 33.2 per cent, compared to 32.2 per cent in the preceding six months.
The majority of these sales were apartments and condominiums at 3,032 units, followed by serviced residences (1,114 units) and double and triple-storey terraces (610 units).
Of the newly launched units, 53 per cent were priced between RM300,001 and RM500,000, and were mostly located in Perak, Pahang, and Negri Sembilan.
Zaini said continued collaboration among the government, financial institutions and the industry is important to ensure that Malaysians who are financially capable of owning a home are able to do so.

"It is equally important for the relevant authorities to review statutory, regulatory and other compliance-related costs, particularly those which may no longer necessary or relevant, as these ultimately add to the cost of housing delivery," he said.

Looking ahead to 2H 2026, developers remain selective, with only 37 per cent of respondents indicating plans to launch. These planned launches involve 18,696 units, the majority of which will be strata units.
The 63 per cent of respondents without new launch plans cited unfavourable market conditions, delays in approval, and a higher number of unsold stocks as their top three reasons.
However, 56 per cent of respondents indicated plans to expand their land banks between July 2026 and June 2027, showing continued investment in long-term development opportunities.

e7d1875fb71cf30e: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit ended higher against major currencies on Wednesday but weakened against the greenback as expectations of further interest rate hikes by the United States Federal Reserve (Fed) continued to support the US dollar.
At 6pm, the ringgit edged down to 4.0780/0825 against the greenback from Tuesday's close of 4.0730/0775.

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said markets expect the Fed to raise interest rates by another 50 basis points this year, providing further support to the US dollar.

"The ringgit actually started the day stronger, reaching RM4.0640 against the US dollar in the morning. But it could not maintain that strength. As the US dollar remained firm, the ringgit weakened to around RM4.0780 in the afternoon.
"Other Asian currencies also showed mixed movements, so the ringgit's performance was not completely isolated," he told Bernama.
At the close, the ringgit traded higher against a basket of major currencies.

It gained against the euro to 4.6522/6573 from 4.6705/6757 at Tuesday's close and advanced vis-à-vis the British pound to 5.4156/4216 from 5.4452/4512. It also strengthened against the Japanese yen to 2.5836/5868 from 2.5958/5988 previously.
The local note traded mixed against its Asean peers.

However, the ringgit declined against the Indonesian rupiah to 228.8/229.2 from 227.7/228.0 and weakened against the Philippine peso to 6.51/6.52 from 6.49/6.50.
8f3f12a9d4ecf7dd: HANGZHOU, Sept 23 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said he remains firm in his decision to resign as Transport Minister.
The Seremban MP said he would hand in his resignation letter upon returning home from China.
“The decision has been made. I will submit the resignation letter to the Prime Minister (Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim) when I return home,” he told reporters briefly after arriving in Hangzhou today.
He is currently accompanying the Prime Minister on a three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou at the invitation of the Chinese government.
Loke offered to resign following a DAP Central Executive Committee (CEC) meeting on Saturday in response to the conditional pardon granted to former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak.
He said the other DAP ministers and deputy ministers would remain in the Unity Government.

Speaking to Malaysian media while travelling from Shanghai to Hangzhou by high-speed train, Anwar said he would not rush into a decision on Loke’s intention to resign as Transport Minister, adding that he wanted to hear Loke’s explanation first.
The Prime Minister added that DAP should not bow to calls from parties he described as having political interests for it to withdraw from the government.
34ad0fe8d6c108b7: ADDIS ABABA: Tigrayan rebels in northern Ethiopia seized control of the key regional airport and battled federal troops in the neighbouring region of Afar, multiple sources told AFP on Wednesday, as long-standing tensions spilled into open conflict.
The Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) fought a devastating civil war with the federal government in 2020-2022 that killed some 600,000 people, according to African Union estimates.
Sporadic clashes in recent months have raised fears of a return to war.

There has been fighting "since last night in Abala and Erebti (in Afar) between TPLF and federal forces. We are expecting it to expand. We just sent a truck with food to help the people displaced," an NGO source in the region told AFP, requesting anonymity.
Abala is located in mountain ranges that mark the border with Tigray. Erebti lies around 100 kilometres (60 miles) further into Afar.
Another humanitarian source confirmed clashes in the two locations, as did a foreign security source in Ethiopia.
A former TPLF senior official told AFP the rebels were in control of Berhale, Erebti, Abala, Megale, Dalul and Konoba in Afar.
The federal forces are "fast-retreating", he added.
Meanwhile, local and security sources said Tigrayan forces were in control of the airport in the regional capital Mekelle.
Ethiopian Airlines said it had suspended flights to three airports in Tigray -- Mekelle, Axum and Shire -- "due to the current situation".

"While we were on our way to the airport for work, our supervisor called the driver and told him that the airport had been taken over by Tigray forces. Since there were no flights, he told us to return home," an employee at Alula Aba Nega Airport in Mekelle told AFP.
The information was confirmed by a foreign security source based in Ethiopia.
A small number of federal police guard the airport and their situation was unknown.
On Sunday, the TPLF announced it had joined a new alliance of anti-government armed groups from across the country.
Ethiopia faces multiple insurgencies, including in its most populous regions, Oromia and Amhara.
The TPLF ruled the whole of Ethiopia from 1991 to 2018 before being sidelined with the rise of Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, eventually triggering the civil war.
The Pretoria Peace Agreement ended the war and maintained an uneasy calm until late 2025, when clashes resumed.
The federal government has since launched drone strikes in Tigray and massed troops at the regional border.
Rights groups have accused the TPLF of a campaign of forced recruitment this year as it prepares for renewed conflict.
The region has not recovered from the last war, with around one million people still displaced and many aspects of the peace agreement unfulfilled.
Ethiopian authorities have accused the TPLF of allying with neighbouring Eritrea, as well as Ethiopian armed groups.
The federal government has a significant military advantage, having ramped up production of military drones since the last conflict.

b95332d84ed98aec: KUALA LUMPUR: Akta baharu menggantikan Akta Universiti dan Kolej Universiti 1971 (Auku) mungkin tidak sempat dibentangkan dalam sidang Parlimen bulan depan kerana libat urus komprehensif sedang diadakan dengan pelbagai pihak.

"Auku membabitkan 44 seksyen dan hanya tujuh seksyen berkaitan mahasiswa. Baki seksyen lain menyentuh aspek penubuhan universiti, tadbir urus dan akademik.

Susulan itu, beliau dilaporkan berkata, kerajaan menyasarkan RUU berkaitan akan dibentangkan di Dewan Rakyat tahun ini.
Auku yang digubal pada 1971 menjadi tumpuan perdebatan mengenai kebebasan mahasiswa melakukan bantahan, berorganisasi dan menyuarakan pandangan mengenai isu politik serta awam.

4bf3877163de49c6: HONG KONG: The trial of the former husband and in-laws of slain Hong Kong socialite and model Abby Choi began on Sept 21, more than three years after her gruesome death shocked the city and made headlines worldwide.

She was also a prominent figure in the fashion world, frequently appearing at Paris Fashion Week and in top publications such as Vogue, Harper's Bazaar, and Elle.

7a4c9436e86e3dc4: KUALA LUMPUR: 2027 Budget, to be tabled on Oct 9, is expected to benefit the construction and building materials sectors, based on current market consensus of RM85 billion to RM90 billion in development expenditure, according to Moomoo.
The online trading and investment platform said the sectors could benefit particularly from contracts involving hospitals, schools and transport infrastructure.
It said beyond traditional construction materials, grid and water infrastructure, renewable energy and energy storage could also benefit from development spending.
"Semiconductors and artificial intelligence-linked names will continue to ride the data centre and National AI Action Plan wave.
"Lastly, targeted cash aids like BUDI95 would support value and affordable consumer stocks by protecting baseline household purchasing power," it said in a statement.
But steel and high-carbon energy producers could face pressure from the proposed carbon tax, which would introduce additional compliance costs.

Moomoo said discretionary consumer stocks may face headwinds from the potential expansion or adjustment of the Sales and Service Tax (SST) framework, as middle-class spending power may come under pressure.
It added that tobacco and alcohol stocks could face pre-Budget uncertainty over potential excise duty increases.
For investors, Moomoo said diversification across sectors will be important, with opportunities spanning Bursa-listed companies and global companies linked to the AI and semiconductor cycle.

Moomoo noted that current market consensus estimates put 2027 Budget's total expenditure at around RM438.9 billion, comprising approximately RM353.1 billion in operating expenditure and RM85.8 billion in development expenditure.
This is broadly in line with the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) 2026-2030, which provides for average development expenditure of RM86 billion annually.

Beyond the headline spending figure, Moomoo said two key policy areas that could influence market sentiment and foreign capital flows are fuel subsidies and fiscal discipline, and taxation and government revenue.

On subsidies, the government's ability to balance rising global energy costs with fiscal discipline will be closely watched, particularly after the BUDI95 basic subsidy quota was restored to 300 litres per month at RM1.99 per litre from Sept 1, benefiting more than 16 million people.
With the 2026 fuel subsidy bill potentially reaching RM40 billion, Moomoo said the government's ability to maintain fiscal discipline while protecting households will remain under scrutiny.
On taxation, the market does not expect major new taxes; the focus is likely to remain on optimising the existing tax framework, including SST and the capital gains tax on unlisted shares.

The increase in the mandatory e-Invoicing threshold from RM1 million to RM3 million in annual revenue from Sept 1 also provides relief for small and medium enterprises (SMEs), while the proposed carbon tax targeting the steel and energy sectors remains an area to watch.

3ae30210c7f46338: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 23 — Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) has retained its position as the world’s fourth most connected international airport while remaining the most connected megahub in Asia-Pacific.
According to OAG’s 2026 Megahubs Index, KLIA’s capacity grew by 6.9 per cent, supported by the expansion of its airline network.

Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) managing director Datuk Mohd Izani Ghani said KLIA’s standing among the world’s most connected megahubs reflected the strength and breadth of its aviation network, supported by airline partners, airport teams and industry stakeholders. However, he said KLIA’s growth was not simply about adding more destinations, with greater connectivity needing to be matched by sufficient capacity and a seamless passenger experience.

“But growth is meaningful only when it is matched by the right experience and the right capacity to support it. That is why our focus at KLIA goes beyond connectivity. We are working across the entire passenger journey to make KLIA more convenient, efficient and welcoming,” he said in a statement today.

To date, KLIA has welcomed seven new scheduled airlines and nine new routes, providing additional connections to destinations including Riyadh, Algeria and Jinan. Malaysia Airlines has also strengthened connectivity with Japan through its new direct Fukuoka-Kuala Lumpur service.

MAHB said the expansion is set to continue with Gulf Air, Hainan Airlines, ZIPAIR and Thai Vietjet scheduled to commence services later this year, while Lufthansa is set to return in October with five weekly flights between Frankfurt and Kuala Lumpur.

Mohd Izani said MAHB aims to further strengthen KLIA’s position as Asia-Pacific’s most connected megahub while ensuring service excellence keeps pace with its expanding network. Among recent improvements are upgraded check-in and self-service bag-drop facilities, enhanced kerbside traffic management through the Vehicle Access Management System (VAMS) and a new e-hailing system at Terminal 1.

MAHB has also introduced additional passenger trolleys, complimentary wheelchairs and baby strollers as well as family-friendly facilities, while the “Calm Room” and “Harimau Playground” have been introduced at Terminal 2. The airport operator said the combination of a stronger network, enhanced passenger experience and continued capacity investment would position KLIA to connect Malaysia with more destinations and travellers worldwide. — Bernama

eeb1d69645bda876: Swedish celebrities will front a national campaign encouraging the public to exercise their rudeness in an effort to drive down rates of cyber scams. According to Polisen, Sweden’s police authority, the country’s cybercriminals profited 5.7 billion SEK ($579.9 million USD) in 2025 alone, and their scams are especially successful when targeting the elderly. “The message is simple: Dare to be rude – it could save you from being scammed,” said the Polisen this week, announcing a relaunch of the campaign with four new faces. Actors Suzanne Reuter, Lennart Jähkel, and Christina Schollin are joined by journalist Claes Elfsberg in the public awareness campaign, which will run through October 11 across print media, social media, and television. “I am part of the police campaign because it is a terrible crime that affects so many people,” said Reuter. “If I can use my voice to help someone not to be scammed, then I want to do it. “Many of us are raised to always be polite and accommodating, and there are many in my generation. But today you have to dare to be a little more questioning. It's not rude – it's self-protection.” Polisen’s national operations leader, Robert Öhman, said fraudsters are skilled social engineers, adept at building trust simultaneously with a sense of stress or urgency. His aim for the campaign is to encourage the public to feel more comfortable with simply hanging up the phone if they feel something might be awry. Telephone-based scams are by far the most common. Typically targeting the over-60s, the Polisen said scammers will often send targets SMS messages under various guises, but always claiming to represent a trusted authority, such as the government or a bank. Unwitting victims then call the telephone number included in the message and are connected to the scammers who read from a prepared script. Like the Netherlands, Sweden is also affected by fake police officer scams. These typically see crooks dress as police officers, offering to collect and safely store valuables, but steal them after the victim transfers them. In these cases, police and campaigners are urging the public to fight their learned social norms and shut the door “at the slightest hesitation.” “The police and other reputable organizations or companies never go to someone's home to collect gold, credit cards or other valuables,” the Polisen said. Officials are not only concerned about the personal losses incurred by victims, but also about the ways in which the stolen funds are used. “The money that the fraudsters get can also help finance other serious crimes,” said Öhman. “In the ongoing operation, we can confirm close cooperation between the organized fraudsters and the pure violent networks. “Therefore, we must both reduce the risk of people being deceived and strike at the criminal actors behind the crimes.” Swedish police and the country’s Post and Telecom Agency (PTS) started working more closely to combat telephone fraud in June. That same month, the Swedish Parliament approved new rules under the Electronic Communications Act compelling providers of number-based services to block suspected fraud communications before they reach the recipient. The amendments came into force as of August 1, and followed previous legislative tweaks that tasked the PTS with blocking spam calls, especially those originating from overseas and spoofing real Swedish numbers. ®

Ninth seed Sanjay Jeeva, who is making his debut in the Asian Games, overcame Abdurakhmonov Muhammadmustafo of Uzbekistan 11-2, 11-4, 11-9 in the second round.
Sanjay, ranked 59th in the world, will face third seed Veer Chotrani of India in the third round.
In the women's competition, defending champion S. Sivasangari and third seed Aira Azman will play their second round matches on Thursday.
World No. 5 Sivasangari, who received a bye in the first round, will face Sri Lanka's Chanithma Sinaly Veera Samiyel for a place in the quarter-finals.
National champion Aira, who also received a bye in the first round, will take on Sana Bahadar of Pakistan in the second round.

14f58d1991f68efd: NEW YORK, Sept 20 — Avery Garcia, known online as “Avery the Poke Kid”, has died at the age of 12 after a long battle with pancreatoblastoma, a rare and aggressive form of childhood pancreatic cancer.

Avery built a large following on social media through his love of Pokémon, sharing videos of card openings, collection showcases and updates on his cancer journey. Despite years of surgeries, treatments and hospital stays, he remained an upbeat presence who inspired fellow Pokémon fans around the world.
In the days before his death, supporters helped Avery reach one of his biggest goals by pushing his YouTube channel past 100,000 subscribers, earning him the platform's Silver Play Button.
The young content creator also shared one final Pokémon card pull with his followers, a moment that resonated deeply with fans who had followed his journey and passion for the franchise.

In a statement posted on social media, Avery's parents said he died on September 18, describing how they spent his final moments together as a family, telling him how much he was loved and how proud they were of him.

Tributes have since poured in from across the Pokémon community, with supporters remembering Avery for his courage, positivity and generosity, including his habit of sharing Pokémon cards with other children undergoing treatment.
“Thank you for loving our little boy,” his parents wrote as they thanked supporters worldwide for their prayers and kindness throughout Avery's battle with cancer.
50d95df3baa88c11: NAGOYA, Sept 23 — National karate exponent C. Shahmalarani delivered gold No. 3 for Malaysia when she won the women’s below 50-kilogramme (kg) kumite event at the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games today.
Competing at her second Asiad, Shahmalarani defeated Hong Kong’s Tsang Yee Ting via a judges’ decision after the final three-minute bout ended 0-0 at the Toyohashi Gymnasium.

The national exponent had earlier defeated Uzbekistan’s Gulshan Alimardanova 3-2 in the semi-finals. It was sweet revenge for Shahmalarani, who lost to Alimardanova in the final of the World Karate Championships in Cairo, Egypt, last year.
“It was a roller-coaster ride (in today’s final) but… I’m so happy right now. I just want to enjoy the moment because the journey (to gold) has been very, very tough.
“But being drawn with the world champion and the world number five, who I have met so many times that we know each other (well)... this is the way to win a medal,” she said when met after the final.
Shahmalarani said her road to the Asiad this time had been a rought one, having had to deal with injuries and several disappointing results in previous competitions.
“And you tend to have a lot of self-doubt, like if I’m on the right path for the Asian Games. It’s the Asiad and the responsibility to delver the goods for the country is on my shoulders,” she said.
Shahmalarani began her Asiad campaign with an 8-0 win over Macau’s Fong Man Wai in the first round before edging Bangladesh’s Saiama Jaman 5-4 in the last eight. — Bernama
91d43949c8f745f6: KUALA LUMPUR: A technician charged with voluntarily causing grievous hurt to a businessman during an assault at a restaurant has been granted RM20,000 bail with one surety.
High Court judge Nurulhuda Nur'aini Mohamad Nor allowed the bail application by Lai Kae Bin, 33.
The court ordered Lai to surrender his passport until the disposal of the case, report weekly to the Kepong police station and refrain from approaching the victim and witnesses.
Earlier, lawyer Muhamad Firdaus Jumaludin applied for bail, saying his client was not a flight risk and needed to care for his ailing mother following his father's death.
Firdaus said a review of closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage showed that Lai's involvement in the incident was minor.
"Some of the footage showed that Lai was not the person who initiated the attack and had attempted to stop it.
"Moreover, the presumption of innocence applies," he said, adding that the prosecution's proposed bail of RM30,000 was excessive.

Deputy public prosecutor Haslida Ismail objected to the bail application, urging the court to consider the severity of the offence, the risk of witness interference and the possibility of the accused absconding.
She also questioned whether the proposed surety, who was not Lai's immediate relative, was sufficient to ensure his compliance with the bail conditions and attendance in court.
"The victim was traumatised by the incident. The prosecution is concerned that the accused might approach or interfere with the victim if released," she said.
Nurulhuda also reminded the surety of his responsibility to ensure that Lai attends court, failing which the bail sum would be forfeited.
Firdaus had previously said Lai had instructed him to seek a lesser charge, as he believed the existing charge under Section 326 of the Penal Code was too serious.
Lai's representation to the Attorney-General's Chambers is still under review.
Lai is one of three men charged with voluntarily causing grievous hurt to businessman Andrew Teh, 47, using dangerous weapons at Restoran Hing Kee Bakuteh in Jalan Kepong at 2am on May 7.
The other two accused are carpenter Wong Weng Luen, 49, and memorial centre worker Wan Ken Fei, 30.
All 3 have pleaded not guilty to the charge.
Wong is currently undergoing psychiatric assessment at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta in Perak following a court order issued last month.
Wan had previously applied for bail but was denied.
The attack allegedly stemmed from an incident in which Teh was accused of staring at a man believed to be intoxicated while dining at the restaurant.
CCTV footage of the several-minute assault later went viral on social media.
The footage showed Teh seated at a table before one of the men approached and began attacking him.
Two others then joined in, initially appearing to restrain their friend before taking part in the assault.
Teh was punched, kicked and struck with various objects, including chairs and a kettle, before managing to escape.

b89ddb49768b49a2: TEHRAN: Iranian airlines were forced to cancel some international flights on Wednesday after the US tightened sanctions on Iran's aviation industry in a new effort to cripple its economy.
A travel agent in Tehran told AFP that flights to Baghdad, Muscat, Qatar, Georgia and Azerbaijan had all been suspended, but routes to multiple other destinations remained available, including China.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced the new measures on Monday as part of an earlier threat to impose "economic D-Day" on Iran, an attempt to force it into submission following their nearly seven-month war.
But Iran's aviation sector has already been a target of sanctions for years, and it remains unclear what the full impact will be and whether other countries will comply.

Even after the new sanctions took effect on Wednesday, a flight from Tehran operated by Mahan Air, one of Iran's biggest carriers, landed in Guangzhou in China, according to tracking data from FlightRadar24.
China on Tuesday said it opposes the US sanctions and called them illegal. A flight to Shanghai was also due to depart on Wednesday, according to Tehran's international airport.
Some flights to Istanbul were also scheduled, though others had been cancelled, the travel agent in Tehran told AFP.
"The situation is unstable and we are no longer selling tickets for the time being for fear of cancellations," the the agent said, requesting anonymity.

A Mahan flight from Kabul was also expected to arrive in Tehran around midday. According to the website for Tehran's international airport, other connections to Turkey and Armenia also remained possible using smaller Iranian airlines, including Varesh.
Flights to Najaf in Iraq and Dubai in the United Arab Emirates were also scheduled.
Bessent on Monday vowed to "shut down" Iranian carriers and punish anyone doing business with them.

"If they land, you cannot provide them with fuel, you cannot provide them with landing services, you cannot sell them tickets or you will be knocked out of the dollar system," he warned other countries.
The restrictions will further complicate the ability of Iranians to travel abroad or return to their country.
Iranian media also reported cancellations, with the Tasnim news agency on Tuesday citing a civil aviation spokesman as saying that Baghdad and Muscat airports "will no longer accept" Iranian flights.
"Other international flights, including Istanbul, will operate as scheduled and as usual, and at present there are no problems with these flights," Tasnim said.
According to Tasnim, Iran's aviation authorities are in talks to reroute Baghdad flights to Najaf, a major destination for Iranian pilgrims.
In Iraq, while the government has not publicly announced plans to enforce the ban, several sources including a senior government official told AFP that Baghdad would comply with the US measures.
The prospect of a suspension of flights between the two countries has sparked concerns from some Iraqi travel agents.
In Najaf, home to one of the most revered Shia Muslim shrines, agent Haidar Shamaa said "most travel companies in the city depend on booking flights" to Iranian airports.
Several travel agencies said panicked clients were calling for updates and were considering switching to land routes, which would mean much longer journeys.
1e2abc08f07dada6: PETALING JAYA: The whole of Sarawak is battling the haze caused by land and forest fires in Indonesia, with the air quality in Serian back to very unhealthy levels.
According to the environment department's air pollutant index (API) portal, the API in Serian stood at 201 as of 6pm.

The rest of Sarawak recorded unhealthy API readings, with the highest reported in Kuching at 185, followed by Samarahan (182), Sri Aman (176), Bintulu (174), Sibu (166), Samalaju (164), Sarikei (164), Miri (161), Mukah (160), the Miri Industrial Training Institute (154), Limbang (153) and Kapit (121).
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality; 51 to 100 moderate; 101 to 200 unhealthy; 201 to 300 very unhealthy; and above 300 hazardous.
The air quality in the rest of the country remained largely moderate, while nine areas in the peninsula recorded good API readings.
2169633bacac2b82: BRUSSELS: The European Commission said Wednesday it has proposed unlocking a first €4.2 billion (US$4.8 billion) for Hungary and remitting it to the bloc's student mobility and research schemes, after Budapest's new government delivered promised reforms.

Prime Minister Peter Magyar launched a reform drive upon winning office this year, aiming to regain access to more than €16 billion that Brussels had frozen over rule-of-law concerns during nationalist leader Viktor Orban's rule.
"Hungary has taken important steps to strengthen the rule of law and protect the Union's financial interests," EU chief Ursula von der Leyen said.
"Today, we are proposing to unlock €4.2 billion and reopen the doors of Erasmus+ and Horizon Europe to Hungarian students and researchers," she said.
"The plan needs to be approved by member states within a month," the commission said.

It cited reforms on public procurement and tackling corruption, including reinforcing the powers of an anti-graft watchdog and the establishment of a comprehensive asset declaration system, among the reasons for the decision.

"With the important steps taken by the government of prime minister Peter Magyar to safeguard EU taxpayers' money, billions of euros can now flow again," said Piotr Serafin, the EU commissioner for budget, anti-fraud and public administration.
540148d4a33acb3d: BUTTERWORTH: A crane operator who received nearly RM47,000 in temporary disability payments for a work-related injury cannot sue his employer for damages arising from the same accident, the sessions court here has ruled.

Sessions court judge Norzafirah Ali said Section 31 of the Employees’ Social Security Act 1969 prevented workers covered by the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) from making a civil claim against their employers over injuries suffered at work.
Norzafirah issued the ruling over a suit filed by Ng Poh Guan, 63, who said he slipped and fell while climbing down a crane at a construction site in Seberang Perai Selatan on Jan 3, 2020.
Ng sued his employer, Great Piling Sdn Bhd, as well as Iconic Construction Sdn Bhd and Iconic Development Sdn Bhd, claiming the three companies were responsible for the accident.

However, the court said he had received RM46,978.66 in temporary disability payments from Perkeso between January 2020 and March 2021, preventing him from suing Great Piling over the same workplace injuries.

Norzafirah noted that the same rule did not automatically protect Iconic Construction and Iconic Development because they were not Ng’s employers, and that he could have succeeded against them had he proven they were responsible for the site or had contributed to the accident.
However, the court found that Iconic Construction only took over the site on Feb 18, 2020, more than a month after the incident, and that Iconic Development was not in charge of the site at the time.
The site was then under a different company, which had hired Great Piling to carry out piling work.
The court said neither Iconic Construction nor Iconic Development had direct control over Ng or the crane, and Ng had, therefore, failed to prove that either company was responsible for his injuries.
Ng's suit against all three companies was dismissed. He was ordered to pay RM5,000 in costs to Great Piling and RM2,500 each to Iconic Construction and Iconic Development.
Lawyer Lim Ee Theng appeared for Ng, while P Paannimalar appeared for Great Piling, and S Parameswaran appeared for Iconic Construction and Iconic Development.
944dd8aa6c91514d: KUALA LUMPUR: Singer and composer Yasin Sulaiman said that his prison stint was a "rather productive" one as he came up with 12 new songs, armed with one pencil and some paper.
Yasin, 51, said that he also identified the singers whom he wanted to perform these songs.
"As for me, I've decided to sing three or four of them. The rest will go to other singers, mostly rising talents, but I can't reveal who they are for now," he said in a news report yesterday.
Yasin memorised the melodies of each song while behind bars and consistently hummed them so that they "sunk" into his head.
"Prison gave me lots of time to improve each song, too," he said, adding that he did the same while at Hospital Bahagia in Tanjung Rambutan, Ipoh.
"In that hospital, I successfully got a laptop computer to ease my work on the songs."
Yasin was discharged from the mental hospital on Sept 2 after spending a year there.
The Mimpi Laila singer was sentenced to life imprisonment and 16 strokes of the rotan for three charges of drug possession by the Shah Alam High Court on Aug 22, 2024.
He was released by the Putrajaya Court of Appeal on April 28, 2025 and placed in Hospital Bahagia where he underwent rehabilitation for a year.
ec63746ac1137d31: PUTRAJAYA: Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor will resist any attempt by Global Royalty Trading SAL to enforce a High Court judgment ordering her to pay RM67.5 million over 43 missing pieces of jewellery.
Rosmah's lawyers from Messrs Reza Rahim & Rajivan in a statement said the wife of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak would continue to pursue her appeal against the June 10 decision.

"Although the Court of Appeal dismissed the application for unconditional stay, nevertheless our client had on June 12 filed an appeal against the High Court's decision," the firm said in a statement.
Rosmah's appeal against the High Court's decision has been fixed for hearing on March 25 next year.
The lawyers said any attempt by Global Royalty to enforce or execute the High Court judgment in the meantime would be "resisted vigorously."

The firm said it was studying the implications of today's Court of Appeal decision and would file any necessary applications either before the High Court or Federal Court to preserve Rosmah's rights pending her appeal.
They said Rosmah had maintained that Global Royalty's claim against her was without basis in fact and law.
This statement came after the appellate court dismissed Rosmah's application for an unconditional stay of the judgment pending her appeal.
A three-member bench chaired by Datuk Seri Mohd Firuz Jaffril unanimously ruled that Rosmah had failed to show sufficient grounds to warrant an unconditional stay.
The other judges on the bench were Datuk Amarjeet Singh and Datuk Aliza Sulaiman.
The court also ordered Rosmah to pay RM30,000 in costs to Global Royalty.
Following the dismissal, the court said Global Royalty was at liberty to take steps to enforce the High Court judgment.
On Aug 12, the High Court had granted Rosmah a conditional stay pending the disposal of her appeal.

Judicial Commissioner Marianne Antoinette Ghani, however, ordered Rosmah to deposit the full judgment sum of RM67,461,027.37 into a joint stakeholders' account held by solicitors for both parties within one month.
Rosmah sought an unconditional stay from the Court of Appeal.

On June 10, High Court judge Datuk Quay Chew Soon ordered Rosmah to pay RM67.5 million to Global Royalty after finding her liable for failing to return 43 pieces of jewellery entrusted to her on a consignment basis.
The court ordered her to pay RM67,461,027.37 within one month.

Quay also dismissed Rosmah's third-party claim against the Inspector-General of Police and the government, rejecting her contention that the jewellery had been seized by the authorities during police raids linked to the 1Malaysia Development Bhd investigations in 2018.

The suit stemmed from 44 pieces of jewellery, including diamond necklaces, earrings, rings, bracelets and a tiara, which Global Royalty claimed were sent to Rosmah for her inspection in February 2018.
The company maintained that the jewellery remained its property and was to be returned if Rosmah did not purchase the items.
Only one of the 44 pieces was recovered, while the whereabouts of the remaining 43 became the subject of the suit.

28b8b726e2d32ca9: KUALA LUMPUR: Marine & General Bhd (M&G) remains cautious on its prospects for the current financial year, maintaining a neutral outlook amid normalising domestic offshore support vessel (OSV) charter rates and more competitive tendering.
For the quarter ended July 31, 2026, M&G posted a net profit of RM6.52 million, while pre-tax profit stood at RM9.6 million on revenue of RM75.6 million.
Sequentially, quarterly performance improved as revenue rose RM8.7 million from RM66.9 million in the preceding quarter and pre-tax profit increased RM5.5 million from RM4.1 million.
The improvement was driven mainly by higher utilisation in the upstream division after drilling activities resumed following the easing of adverse weather conditions in the South China Sea.

However, year-on-year performance was weaker, with revenue down RM23.8 million and pre-tax profits falling RM13.8 million, reflecting lower vessel availability and moderating domestic drilling activity.
The upstream division remained the group's main revenue contributor, accounting for 79 per cent of quarterly revenue.
Its revenue rose 15.5 per cent quarter-on-quarter to RM61.6 million, while fleet utilisation improved to 75 per cent from 69 per cent.
The division swung to a pre-tax profit of RM9.35 million from a loss of RM380,000 previously.
This was helped partly by lower depreciation following M&G's revision of its offshore support vessels' estimated useful life from 20 to 25 years.
Year-on-year, however, upstream revenue fell from RM85.5 million, and pre-tax profit declined from RM22 million, as several vessels underwent mandatory docking and repairs.
The downstream division remained stable, with revenue at RM13.8 million and fleet utilisation at 89 per cent.
Its pre-tax profit eased to RM1.2 million from RM1.7 million a quarter earlier, partly due to higher depreciation following the acquisition of a clean petroleum product tanker in December 2025.
M&G said medium-term demand for offshore support vessels remains supported by exploration and development activities in Malaysia.
It warned of near-term margin pressure from competitive tenders, higher drilling costs and stricter environmental requirements.
The group will focus on operational efficiency, vessel availability and fleet optimisation, while continuing to assess opportunities in its services business.

2012ef42b9dffdce: ALOR GAJAH, Sept 23 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is expected to announce its candidates for the Melaka state election one to two weeks before nomination day, said Prime Minister’s political secretary Datuk Azman Abidin.
He said the move would allow PH to make early preparations instead of waiting until the last minute to finalise its candidates.
“This time, we are better prepared to name our candidates,” he told reporters after visiting beneficiaries under the Ziarah Kasih programme at the Kuala Linggi state constituency here today.

Azman said the candidate selection process would be left to the party leadership, taking into account lists submitted by party divisions, state leaders and the grassroots before the final decision is made.
Earlier, Azman visited seven recipients under the Ziarah Kasih programme, including a single mother with two children who is unable to work after being involved in a road accident.

Azman said the Ziarah Kasih programme was among the activities carried out by the Political Secretary’s Office and would continue in several other areas in Melaka, including the Jasin parliamentary constituency next week. — Bernama
edddb5f159ca6f6a: KUALA LUMPUR: As the Negaraku echoed through Toyohashi Gymnasium and the Jalur Gemilang rose highest for the first time at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Tuesday, Malaysian karate stood tall — thanks to the unheralded Adeola Fay Robert.
The journey of the 20-year-old from Tambunan, Sabah to the top of the Asiad podium is a story of discipline, sacrifice and a family that taught her to strive.
Raised in a family of educators — her parents and siblings are all teachers — education and community service were not just values but a way of life for Adeola.
Adeola embodied that commitment early, scoring an impressive 7As in her Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia examinations.
She was pursuing her Form 6 studies in Sabah when national karate coach R. Sharmendran spotted her potential following a promising silver medal win at the 2024 Sarawak Malaysia Games (Sukma).
Joining the high-performance programme at Bukit Jalil meant a life-changing decision of leaving her family and crossing the South China Sea.
"I knew an opportunity like this doesn't come often," Adeola said.
"Even though it was a tough decision to make, I wanted to challenge myself and chase my dreams in karate."
The transition to the elite training programme at Bukit Jalil demanded immense mental resilience.
While adapting to a gruelling training regimen at Bukit Jalil, Adeola also held firm to her studies at the Institute of Teacher Education Kampus Ilmu Khas in Cheras.
There, she learned patience for educating children with special needs — and mastered the explosive combat of elite karate.
"At first, my family was worried because I had to be far away from them," she admitted.
"The biggest hurdle was being away from my family and adapting to a much more intensive training regimen. But over time, I grew stronger both physically and mentally."
That blend of intellectual sharpness and physical conditioning reached its peak on the continental stage.
Entering the gold-medal match on her Asian Games debut, Adeola maintained absolute tactical discipline, anchoring herself in her preparation and her coach's final words of encouragement.
"I just kept reminding myself to trust my abilities and give it everything I had," she said.
"My coach told me to stay locked in and trust myself."
The unfancied Adeola ended up delivering Malaysia's first gold medal at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games after beating Iran's Fatemeh Zahra Saeidabadi 6-4 in the women's kumite Under-55kg final.
Standing atop the podium in the Japanese city of Toyohashi validated every early morning training session and every sacrifice made away from home.
"I felt an overwhelming sense of pride and emotion," she recalled.
"Seeing the Jalur Gemilang raised to the highest point was an immense honour. This gold means everything because every sacrifice and hard work over the years has finally paid off.
"I hope this achievement makes my family, my coaching team, my friends, and all Malaysians proud."

Dedicating her victory to her family, national coaches and supporters, Adeola views this success not as a final destination, but as a foundation for greater heights — including her ultimate dream of competing on the Olympic stage.

Her story is more than a medal. It is a family of teachers who raised a champion, a young woman who refused to choose between the classroom and the gruelling training, and a national system that believed in both.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd
02dec28ccd29b40a: KUALA LUMPUR: MARC Ratings has revised the outlook on JB Cocoa Sdn Bhd's RM500 million sukuk to positive from stable, while affirming the rating at A+IS.
JB Cocoa is a key wholly-owned manufacturing subsidiary of Singapore-listed JB Foods Ltd, which provided a corporate guarantee for the sukuk.
Therefore, MARC's assessment considers JB Foods' consolidated credit profile, given the operational and financial linkages within the group.
The positive outlook reflects MARC's expectation that JB Cocoa will sustain its earnings strength while managing the impact of cocoa price volatility on working capital and liquidity.
The group remained resilient amid exceptionally high and volatile cocoa prices, supported by disciplined risk management, cost-plus pricing arrangements and hedging practices.
For FY26 ended March 31, JB Cocoa's operating profit margin more than doubled to 9.52 per cent from 4.03 per cent in the previous 15-month period.
Leverage also remained manageable despite higher borrowings to fund cocoa bean inventories.
Debt-to-equity improved to 0.96 times from 0.99 times.
Cash flow from operations turned negative during FY26, mainly due to working capital movements, including the settlement of cocoa bean payables.
However, JB Cocoa's liquidity remained adequate, supported by RM195.7 million in cash, substantial banking facilities and available capacity under the sukuk.
Grinding volumes declined to 154,090 tonnes from 164,535 tonnes in FY25, reflecting weaker global cocoa grinding activity as customers shifted to smaller, more frequent orders amid elevated prices.

MARC said JB Foods' upcoming Ivory Coast facility, which will add 60,000 tonnes of capacity and lift total grinding capacity to 270,000 tonnes, should strengthen sourcing and geographic diversification while improving access to European and US markets.
c5294b5033b90756: PAPAR: Two students were charged in the Court for Children today in connection with a bullying case last September.
The two, aged 16 and 17, pleaded guilty to their respective charges before magistrate Zuraini Ali Musa during closed-door proceedings.
The court fixed Oct 29 for re-mention pending probation reports on the two students.
Until then, they were released on RM3,000 bail each without deposit.
It is learnt that the 17-year-old was charged under Section 323 of the Penal Code with voluntarily causing hurt to two junior students.
The 16-year-old, meanwhile, was charged under Section 507B of the Penal Code with an offence involving one of the junior students.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Kareena Kaur Gill Karamjit Singh prosecuted, while both students were unrepresented.
Lawyer Nurshalilah Fauzan Mailin held a watching brief for one of the junior students.
In September last year, a Form Two student at a school in Kinarut was kicked by a senior student, allegedly for being late to return to his hostel room.
Following the incident, the victim's mother lodged a police report at the Papar district police headquarters on Sept 9.

94bbd83694fb24a4: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — Bursa Malaysia closed lower on Wednesday, weighed down by profit-taking in selected heavyweights and weaker sentiment towards petrochemical stocks as oil prices continued to slide, said an analyst.
At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) eased 7.07 points, or 0.42 per cent, to 1,676.43, from Tuesday’s close of 1,683.50.

cbdb1eed505e8f11: AICHI: Wushu exponent Clement Ting erased the disappointment of three years ago in style after securing a bronze medal in the men's daoshu-gunshu event at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Wednesday.
Making the achievement even sweeter, Clement also created history by becoming the first Malaysian athlete to win a medal in the daoshu-gunshu event at the Asian Games.
Clement scored 9.690 points in daoshu and 9.713 in gunshu for a combined total of 19.403 at the Aichi Prefectural Martial Arts Hall.
China's Gao Xiao Bin claimed the gold medal with 19.582 points, scoring 9.786 in daoshu and 9.796 in gunshu.
South Korea's Lee Ha Sung took silver with 19.406 points, after scoring 9.706 in daoshu and 9.700 in gunshu.
For Clement, the achievement was particularly meaningful after he finished fifth overall on his Asian Games debut at Hangzhou 2022.
The 28-year-old said his experience at the previous edition helped him approach this year's competition with greater confidence and composure.
"I'm very happy because this is the second time I have represented Malaysia at the Asian Games. I'm very proud because the level of competition at the Asian Games is extremely high," said Clement.
"This medal proves that all the hard work has not been in vain. Thank you to everyone who has supported me."
Clement said confidence was a crucial factor in delivering his best performance, as failing to maintain it could affect his focus during competition.
"Daoshu and gunshu are very difficult events. Malaysia had never won an Asian Games medal in this event, so I'm extremely proud to have brought home the bronze today.
"Confidence is very important. If you lack confidence, you lose focus.
"At the previous Asian Games, I finished fifth, but this time I came with more experience and confidence, and that helped me today," he added.
6982f5b7d4f7ceab: WARSAW: The top diplomats of EU member Poland and Russian-allied Belarus met on the margins of the UN General Assembly in the first high-level meeting between the neighbours in a decade, with Warsaw saying Wednesday it saw potential for warming ties.
Minsk-Warsaw relations have been essentially frozen for years - over political repression in Belarus, a migrant crisis at the border and Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
Tensions have run high for years between Nato member Poland and reclusive Belarus, ruled by president Alexander Lukashenko since 1994.
Polish foreign minister Radoslaw Sikorski told Warsaw's TVP TV station he met his Belarusian counterpart Maxim Ryzhenkov on the UN's "neutral territory".
"We have, more than in the past, a normalised situation on the border," he said.
"We also have the liberations of prisoners, including Andrzej Poczobut," Sikorski added, referring to a Polish-Belarusian journalist freed by Minsk this year.
"So the neighbours have more reasons to try to stabilise their relations," he said.
The ministers met as US president Donald Trump's administration has re-opened a dialogue with Minsk, easing some sanctions in exchange for prisoner releases.
"This is the first, introductory meeting, but meetings are also taking place at other levels," Sikorski said.
"We will soon be opening a new embassy building in Minsk. When a neighbour wishes to thaw and improve relations, Poland is always first to agree," he said.

Quoted by state news agency Belta, Minsk's foreign ministry said the meeting "focused on assessing the state of Belarusian-Polish ties and paths for their further development in the interests of the peoples of both countries".
Belarus suppressed mass anti-Lukashenko protests in 2020, with hundreds still in prison and thousands driven into exile, mostly to Poland.
In 2022, Minsk allowed Moscow to use its territory to invade Ukraine.
Poland - which borders Belarus, Russia and Ukraine - has also accused Minsk of orchestrating a migrant crisis at its border.
Warsaw has built a wall along the border and human rights groups accuse it of violating the rights of migrants through systemic "pushbacks".
The last time there was a high-level meeting between the neighbours was in 2016, when then Polish prime minister Mateusz Morawiecki visited Minsk.

b4fe1dad4fded580: PETALING JAYA: Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) has sought to allay concerns over its move to shoulder the burden of additional electricity subsidy for households, which resulted in a dip in its share price.

During an analyst briefing yesterday, the national power utility company described its decision to absorb additional surcharges under the automatic fuel adjustment (AFA) mechanism as a “one-off corporate contribution”.

“Management reiterated its decision to absorb an estimated RM120-150 million of AFA-related costs from September to December 2026 as a one-off corporate contribution aimed at cushioning households from higher electricity bills,” said TA Securities in a post-briefing note today.
However, TNB does not discount the possibility of stepping in to assist consumers again if a similar situation arises in the future, considering its role as a GLC, it added.

The government announced last Thursday that households consuming 800 kilowatt-hour (kWh) of power or less monthly will now be spared the surcharge under the AFA system. The exemption was previously provided only to those using under 600kWh each month.
TA also said the government is working on a more permanent solution to address the current AFA design gap although there is “not much clarity yet on this new structure”.

It said TNB highlighted that the AFA framework applies the same rate across the board unlike the previous imbalance cost pass-through (ICPT) mechanism, which allows for cross subsidisation and potentially greater protection for domestic consumers and SMEs.

Under the ICPT mechanism that was replaced in June 2025 by the AFA system, the final tariff to be paid by consumers was adjusted every six months in the form of rebates or surcharges on top of the base tariff.
TA maintained its “hold” call on TNB with a target price of RM13.80.
RHB Research said the TNB management affirmed that the subsidy is one-off, with the protection threshold reverting back to 600kWh in January 2027.
It said the financial impact might be less severe than expected, with TNB stating the RM150 million allocation is premised on a “high case” assumption for fuel prices and foreign exchange in Q4.
“As TNB’s share price has declined by 12% from the recent high, we advise investors to accumulate the stock on share price weakness.

“We expect TNB to report stronger second half earnings as we forecast the effective tax rate to decline to 18% in Q4, which will more than offset the allocation for the electricity subsidies,” it added.
RHB kept its “buy” call on the stock with a TP of RM16.50, a 25% upside to the current price.
TNB's shares closed four sen or 0.3% higher at RM13.14, giving it a market capitalisation of RM76.59 billion. The stock has fallen 4.6% year to date.

f75b179e941b7ea3: JAKARTA, Sept 23 — Indonesian police have identified a body found in Bengkulu as crew member Surakman, one of eight people, including five journalists, who went missing while covering the Anak Krakatau eruption earlier this month.
